picks.title: Black Forest Labs launches FLUX 3, generating images and 20-second video with audio
picks.excerpt: Black Forest Labs unveiled FLUX 3, a new generative model that produces both still images and up to 20-second video clips with audio, extending the FLUX line from image generation into audiovisual output for creative work. It ships in limited release to start.
picks.rationale: Major model release extending FLUX from stills into 20-second audiovisual output — directly widens the generative toolkit designers can reach for; reputable source, high novelty.

picks.title: Chaos just fixed one of the biggest problems with gaussian splats — you can finally relight them
picks.excerpt: Chaos has cracked one of the biggest limitations of Gaussian splats: relighting. Captured splat scenes can now react to new lighting inside a production render pipeline, closing a long-standing gap between neural capture and traditional CG lookdev.
picks.rationale: Relightable splats close a real production gap between neural capture and CG lookdev — actionable for render/lookdev artists; distinct Chaos release, not a repeat of prior splat items.

picks.title: The aggressively mediocre fight: the battle we have with AI and creativity
picks.excerpt: Designer Chris R Becker on the daily battle creatives face with AI — how leaning on generative tools can pull work toward the 'aggressively mediocre,' and what designers must do to push past the default output.
picks.rationale: A workflow-level take on resisting default generative output — changes how a designer approaches AI-assisted work tomorrow; adds category spread beyond render.

picks.title: How to Make a Landing Page That Doesn't Look AI-Generated (7 Concrete Fixes)
picks.excerpt: A practical designer's guide with seven concrete fixes for making AI-assisted landing pages stop looking generic — the spacing, type, imagery and copy tells that give away 'AI-generated' work and how to correct them.
picks.rationale: Seven concrete, apply-tomorrow fixes for de-genericizing AI-assisted UI — highly actionable and hands-on; distinct from the prior anti-slop 'Hallmark' piece.
